title: Identification Equations for Screening Thalassaemia Trait in Pregnancy
author: Yu-wei Yang1
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.irmcd46
materials: During the period from January 2015 to September 2016, all pregnant women were enrolled when they attended for their first antenatal care visit. The recruiting procedure of the patients with IDA or α-TT or β-TT is as following: ⑴ At first, all pregnant women would be asked to fill in a antenatal care questionnaire including food intake, underlying diseases, history of blood loss, current medications, family history of anemia and other demographic data, such as age, sex, height and weight. ⑵ Then all pregnant women would be collected their whole blood samples to measure RBC and reticulocyte parameters by XN-9000 automatic machine (Sysmex, Japan). The RBC parameters include 6 indicators: RBC#, Hb, MCV, MCH, mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC) and RBC distributing width (RDW). The reticulocyte parameters include 7 indicators: reticulocyte counts, percentage of reticulocytes (Ret%), low fluorescence ratio (LFR), medium fluorescence ratio (MFR), high fluorescence ratio (HFR), immature reticulocytes fluorescence ratio (IRF) and hemoglobin content of reticulocytes (Ret-He). ⑶ According to hemoglobin level 4% (in practical work we selected the critical value as 3.5%) would be performed gene analysis. ⑸ All the pregnant women with microcytic hypochromic anemia would be collected their serum samples to make a ferritin measurement. Inclusion criteria: ① All subjects must be with haemoglobin (Hb) <110g/L and decreased MCV and/or MCH. ② TT carriers must be with any gene deficiency of hemoglobin by gene analysis. ③ The patients with IDA must be with ferritin <14μg/L, and without any gene deficiency of hemoglobin. Exclusion criteria: The subjects with a history of infection or inflammation or underlying medical conditions within one month were excluded. In fact, total 4826 pregnant women were enrolled in this study. 925 subjects were diagnosed as anemia, and furthermore only 564 subjects were diagnosed as microcytic hypochromic anemia without a history of infection or inflammation or underlying medical conditions within one month. By the recruiting procedure, 105 α-TT carriers and 143 β-TT carriers and 177 pregnant women with IDA were recruited.

steps.title: Divide Subjects into Study Groups
steps.instruction: Perform random sampling of patients with α-TT, β-TT, or IDA and divide them into a development group and a validation group.

substeps.instruction: Assign 174 cases to the development group (75 IDA, 42 α-TT, 57 β-TT).
Assign 251 cases to the validation group (102 IDA, 63 α-TT, 86 β-TT).

steps.title: Develop Identification Equations
steps.instruction: Use logistic regressions and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses to create two identification equations based on the development group.

substeps.instruction: Develop logit-P1 to distinguish IDA from TT using RBC#, Ret%, and IRF parameters.
Develop logit-P2 to distinguish α-TT from β-TT using MCHC, Ret%, and MRF parameters.

steps.title: Screen for Thalassaemia Trait (TT)
steps.instruction: Apply the logit-P1 equation to classify the patient.

substeps.instruction: If logit-P1 ≥ 0.84, classify as a TT carrier.

steps.title: Distinguish α-TT from β-TT
steps.instruction: Apply the logit-P2 equation to patients identified as TT carriers.

substeps.instruction: If logit-P2 < 0.41, classify as an α-TT carrier.
If logit-P2 ≥ 0.41, classify as a β-TT carrier.

steps.title: Apply Supplementary RBC# Criteria
steps.instruction: Use RBC# as a supplementary criterion to refine the distinction between TT and IDA for cases initially diagnosed as IDA.

steps.title: Validate and Compare Indices
steps.instruction: Validate the equations and compare them against 12 previously published hematological indices using the validation group.

substeps.instruction: Construct ROC curves for all 14 formulas.
Calculate Area Under the Curve (AUC), Youden index (YI), specificity (Spe), sensitivity (Sen), likelihood ratio positive (LRP), and likelihood ratio negative (LRN).
Compare diagnostic values under the proposed criterion versus the optimum criterion (OC) obtained from the validation group.
Contrast rates of missed and correct diagnoses and calculate the kappa coefficient between identification results and clinical diagnosis.
